To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the immune system is an important component of the body’s natural defenses against cancer; (2) many of the most common cancer chemopreventive agents have immunomodulatory effects; and (3) immunomodulation may be an important mechanism of action by which these agents prevent cancer.

1) common chemopreventive agents including NSAIDs, bisphosphonate, and anti-estrogens may enhance immunosurveillance by enhancing dendritic cell function, reversing the immunosuppressive effects of Tregs, and/or activating effector T cells; 2) the effects of these agents on immunosurveillance may be mediated by their anti-inflammatory and/or anti-angiogenic effects; and 3) the effects of chemoprevention may be

common cancer prevention agents such as aspirin, aromatase, bisphosphonate, and COX-2 inhibitor, mediate their effects in part by enhancing the endogeneous immune system to prevent the emergence of premalignant lesions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the immune system in cancer prevention.
the development of new and improved chemoprevention approaches for breast, lung, colon, and prostate cancer.
the development of new methods for the prevention and treatment of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immune system plays a critical role in cancer development.
the immune system is an important player in chemoprevention, but the mechanisms are complex and still need further investigation.
the use of chemoprevention drugs in the prevention of cancer, especially in the early stages of the disease, has a positive effect on the patient's survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the immunomodulation of cancer prevention agents is an important component of the mechanism of action for these agents, and that this mechanism is an important consideration in the development of new cancer prevention agents.
the immune system is an integral component of cancer chemopreventive agents.
cancer prevention is a very important part of the cancer control continuum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune system has a major role in cancer prevention.
there is a strong rationale for using immunotherapy in combination with common chemopreventive agents.
many of the chemoprevention drugs that we use to treat cancer patients and that we use to prevent cancer in high-risk individuals are also modulating the immune system.
